page.layout: One page of text in a single column; running head at top with page number at top left; a small marginal mark at left beside line 'compensationis'; no notes beyond this.

main_text.p: nunciare: vbi autem obligatio siue debitum, ibi meritum est, quamobrem bona opera nostra merentur. Respondeo paucis: Dei justitia quidem postulat vt bona opera Spiritus Sancti (nam de his loquitur) compensentur: sed hoc fit non ratione ipsorum operum, etiā sanctissimorum, cum in ijs perpetuò sit aliqua imperfectio, sed ratione meriti Christi fide apprehensi à persona ea quæ bene operata est. Quoties ergo legimus in Scriptura de mercede siue compensatione, vel bonorum operum personæ, vel personæ ipsius quæ bene operatur, toties in mentem nobis venire debet Christus, ipsiusque meritum, ad quod mercedis siue compensationis nomen proprie est relatum. Nam eæ omnes improprie locutiones sunt, in quibus merces vitæ æternæ, vel omnino gratia Dei refertur, vel ad opera personæ, vel ad personam ipsam operantem. In his enim omnibus Metonymia aliqua est, qua ex effectis causa significatur.

p.i: 11 Cupimus autem vt vnusquisque uestrum idem ostendat studium ad plenam spei persuasionem ad finem usque.

main_text.p: Cupimus autem) Tertia pars capitis: arrepta occasione ex proximo loco, adhortatur ad perseverantiam in bonis operibus, siue studium bonorum operum: simulque dehortatur à segnitie, quæ contraria est studio bonorum operum.

page.notes: Lower part of page: the last word 'perum.' (likely 'perum.' as printed, possibly 'operum.') is set at the right under the text. Some words in the Greek-like italic line are uncertain; the italic line 11 is printed in Hebrew-like/Greek-like letterforms and is transcribed approximately: [?] marks indicate doubtful readings. Original printed text at line 11 reads "Cupimus autem vt vnusquisque uestrum idem ostendat studium ad plenam spei persuasionem ad finem usque." with doubtful letters.
